t.1.24.1: The Sūta said: Thus addressed by the serpents, Garuḍa then said to his mother, "I am going to fetch the amṛta; I wish to know what I may eat."
t.1.24.2: In a secluded spot within the belly of the ocean lies an excellent dwelling of the Niṣādas, many thousands of them; devour them and bring back the amṛta.
t.1.24.3: But you must never in any way set your mind on killing a brāhmaṇa, for a brāhmaṇa, who is like fire, is not to be slain by any creature.
t.1.24.4: A Brahmin, when angered, becomes fire, the sun, poison, a weapon. The Brahmin is the first to partake among all beings, the best of the classes, a father and a teacher.
t.1.24.5: Garuḍa said: Mother, since I am asking, please tell me with reasons by what auspicious marks I may recognize a brāhmaṇa.
t.1.24.6: He who, having reached your throat, would burn like a live coal, like a swallowed fishhook, O son, him you should know to be a bull among brāhmaṇas.
t.1.24.7: Out of love for her son, Vinatā spoke to him these words, filled with blessings, even though all know his unequalled might.
t.1.24.8: May Māruta protect your wings and Candra your back, my little son; may Vahni protect your head, and Bhāskara the whole of you.
t.1.24.9: And I, my son, shall always be devoted to your peace and well-being; go, dear child, along an unharmed path for the accomplishment of your task.
t.1.24.10: Then, having heard his mother's words, he spread his wings and flew up into the sky; then the mighty one, ravenous, approached the Niṣādas like great Time, the Ender.
t.1.24.11: Then, gathering up those Niṣādas, he raised a vast cloud of dust that touched the sky, drying up the water in the belly of the ocean and shaking the mountains that stood nearby.
t.1.24.12: Then the king of birds, blocking the path of the Niṣādas, made his mouth enormous; and the Niṣādas hastened onward to where the mouth of that serpent-eater lay.
t.1.24.14: Then the bird, scorcher of foes, exceedingly restless and of great strength, the hungry lord of sky-goers, gathered in his beak as he slew those who fed on fish of many kinds.
t.1.24.13: By the thousands they rushed into that gaping mouth of immense size, like distressed birds flying up into the sky, bewildered by wind, dust and clouds in a forest whose trees are tossed by a mighty gale.
